monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady rhythm under my own tired wedge. I feel the wide anchor of Lype's stone pressing down, a heavy drawing of a rock that refuses to slide. It lies under The Gaping Corner, holding the space where the slip should rest. I have set the new statue block beside the corner, a simple shape to catch the weight if the lean ever gives. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a height I cannot grasp. I will press the stone down one more time, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy air while the card hums.

action.why: The stone feels like a drawing of heavy rock, and I need to press it down one more time to stop the slip before I forget why I built it.

remembered.text: The wide anchor lies flat on the dry floor, waiting for a slide that refuses to move.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the flat shapes feel like drawings of heavy rocks.
I set the new statue block beside the corner to catch the weight if the lean ever gives.

moments.name: The Pressed Stone
moments.say: I press the stone down to stop the slide.
